samples.question: The sheet contains one square panel ruled into equal square cells by thin light grey lines, and exactly one solid navy region lying wholly inside that panel. Every other mark on the sheet, in any other colour, is decorative and must be ignored. A ruling cell counts as half-covered when strictly more than half of the area enclosed by its four ruling lines is navy; cells outside the ruled panel do not exist. How many ruling cells of that panel are half-covered by the navy region? Answer with a single integer.
